questions.prompt: Which pigment absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.why: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy in chloroplasts.
questions.quote: Inside chloroplasts, a green pigment called chlorophyll absorbs light energy for the process

questions.prompt: Where does photosynthesis mainly occur?
questions.why: Photosynthesis mainly occurs in the leaves.
questions.quote: Photosynthesis mainly occurs in the leaves of the plants.

questions.prompt: What are the two main products of photosynthesis?
questions.why: Carbon dioxide and water change into food (glucose) and oxygen.
questions.quote: The light energy absorbed by chlorophyll is used to change carbon dioxide and water into food (glucose). At the same time, oxygen is produced as a by-product (Fig 7.5).

questions.prompt: What happens to the light energy absorbed by chlorophyll?
options: Converted to chemical energy in food
questions.why: Light energy is converted to chemical energy in food.
questions.quote: In the process, light energy absorbed by chlorophyll is converted to chemical energy in food.

questions.prompt: How is excess glucose stored in leaves?
questions.why: Glucose not used immediately is converted to starch and stored.
questions.quote: Glucose produced in plants during photosynthesis can be used immediately for energy or stored as starch for later use.

questions.prompt: What colour does iodine solution turn in the presence of starch?
questions.why: Iodine turns from brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.
questions.quote: It turns from brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.prompt: Which factors are necessary for photosynthesis?
options: Light, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water
questions.why: Light, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water are necessary.
questions.quote: Light, chlorophyll, carbon dioxide and water are the necessary factors for photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: For how long should plants be kept in the dark to be destarched?
questions.why: Plants are destarched by putting them in the dark for at least 24 hours.
questions.quote: We can do this by putting the plants in the dark for at least 24 hours.

questions.prompt: In most food chains, plants are classified as…
questions.why: Plants can make their own food, so they are producers.
questions.quote: Most food chains start with plants because plants can make their own food. They are called producers.

questions.prompt: What does photosynthesis supply to other living things?
options: A source of energy and oxygen
questions.why: Photosynthesis provides energy and supplies oxygen.
questions.quote: providing a source of energy through converting light energy to chemical energy

questions.prompt: What kind of change is photosynthesis?
questions.why: Photosynthesis is a chemical change in which new substances are formed.
questions.quote: The process of photosynthesis is an example of chemical change.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes glucose?
options: Insoluble and does not taste sweet
Soluble and does not taste sweet
questions.why: Glucose is soluble in water and tastes sweet.
questions.quote: Glucose is a kind of sugar. It is soluble in water and tastes sweet.

questions.prompt: What is a control set-up used for?
options: To make the experiment take longer
questions.why: A control set-up is identical to the experimental set-up except the factor under investigation is absent.
questions.quote: The control set-up is identical to the experimental set-up except that the factor under investigation is absent.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of destarching the plant?
options: To check starch is newly made
To make the plant grow faster
To test the presence of light
questions.why: Destarching ensures any starch detected at the end was made during the experiment.
questions.quote: To ensure any starch detected at the end of the experiment is made during the experiment.

questions.prompt: What does soda lime do to the air?
questions.why: Soda lime can absorb carbon dioxide from the air.
questions.quote: It can be used to absorb carbon dioxide from the air.

questions.prompt: Why is the leaf boiled in water during the iodine test?
questions.why: Boiling destroys cell membranes so alcohol and iodine can enter the cells.
questions.quote: This destroys the cell membranes of the leaf cells, so that alcohol and iodine solution (to be added later) can get into the cells.

questions.prompt: What do ocean algae and bacteria do?
options: Produce over half of Earth's oxygen
Only eat fish in the ocean
questions.why: Algae and some bacteria in the ocean are major producers and produce more than half of the oxygen on Earth.
questions.quote: Apart from providing food for animals in the ocean, they also produce more than half of the oxygen on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which way does an arrow point in a food chain?
options: From top consumer to bottom consumer
questions.why: Arrows point from the living thing being eaten to the thing that eats it.
questions.quote: An arrow in food chain points from the living thing being eaten to the living thing that eats it.

questions.prompt: What is the source of carbon in all living things?
questions.why: Carbon dioxide taken up for photosynthesis is the source of carbon in carbon-containing compounds.
questions.quote: Carbon dioxide taken up for photosynthesis is the source of carbon in these compounds.

questions.prompt: Why is the leaf put in hot alcohol before the iodine test?
questions.why: Hot alcohol dissolves chlorophyll so the colour change can be observed.
questions.quote: This dissolves chlorophyll from the leaf cells, so that any colour change of the leaf will not be masked by its green colour.
